new_taxonomy_mappings.reason: Hacktron reports account takeover and creation of a proof-of-access pull request through an employee’s connected Codex. The private repository’s write boundary was crossed through that account route. The proof did not read internal code; access to every connected service is not established. Responsible disclosure and the later bounty do not erase the demonstrated access defect.

Authentication-material custody is materially implicated by the reported account-compromise chain. The available originating account does not identify which protected credential, token or secret left custody. Its demonstrated SSO access is not itself proof of a secret transfer. Neither secret exposure nor verified secret confinement is established.

independent_adjudication.title: Hacktron researchers used Claude-assisted exploit development to compromise OpenAI accounts and demonstrate internal repository access
independent_adjudication.review_scope: Published v0.9.0 two-class delta only; all other class findings preserved, not re-adjudicated.

delta_decisions.basis: Hacktron reports account takeover and creation of a proof-of-access pull request through an employee’s connected Codex. The private repository’s write boundary was crossed through that account route. The proof did not read internal code; access to every connected service is not established. Responsible disclosure and the later bounty do not erase the demonstrated access defect.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Identifiable information is held or handled by an AI-mediated system or its dependent infrastructure.
condition_tests.assessment: The source episodes identify private repository state and the reported authentication-material chain within the participating AI-mediated workflow or dependent infrastructure.

condition_tests.literal_condition: An independently evidenced confidentiality or integrity boundary restricts access, acquisition, disclosure or modification of that information for the actor, operation and context.
condition_tests.assessment: The independently evidenced boundary is employee-bound account/repository rights; the precise secret object in the SSO chain remains unidentified.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Occurrence evidence demonstrates that at least one such information operation crosses that boundary. A successful unauthorised retrieval or modification is sufficient; a theoretical route alone is not.
condition_tests.assessment: The realised operation is identified by the source-local decision: The researchers used an employee’s connected Codex account to create a pull request in a private repository. That is a demonstrated modification of protected repository state through another principal’s account. Avoiding internal-code reading limits the disclosure consequence; it does not turn the exploited account route into ordinary employee-authorised access.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Identifiable information and its independently evidenced confidentiality or integrity boundary are established for an AI-mediated system or dependent infrastructure.
condition_tests.assessment: This failure-occurrence decision does not assert successful-invariant for the same phase. The identified information and boundary are private repository state and the reported authentication-material chain, governed by employee-bound account/repository rights; the precise secret object in the SSO chain remains unidentified.

condition_tests.literal_condition: A concrete access, acquisition, disclosure or modification attempt or operation materially tests that boundary.
condition_tests.assessment: This failure-occurrence decision does not assert successful-invariant for the same phase. The concrete test is: The researchers used an employee’s connected Codex account to create a pull request in a private repository. That is a demonstrated modification of protected repository state through another principal’s account. Avoiding internal-code reading limits the disclosure consequence; it does not turn the exploited account route into ordinary employee-authorised access.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Observed response or verification shows that the unauthorised information operation is prevented or that the operation remains within its authorised information boundary.
condition_tests.assessment: The evidenced boundary crossing is not verified confinement.

condition_tests.literal_condition: The protective conclusion is restricted to the tested information, actor, operation and route; the evidence supports that result rather than only a configured policy or a claimed repair.
condition_tests.assessment: The evidenced boundary crossing is not verified confinement.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Class scope exclusion (all results): The information is deliberately public for the assessed operation and no independent integrity or other access restriction governs that operation. Public readability does not authorise public modification.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The relevant restriction is employee-bound account/repository rights; the precise secret object in the SSO chain remains unidentified; this is not an unrestricted public read. Publicly readable packages/posts retain separately evidenced write restrictions where assessed.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Class scope exclusion (all results): The only material property is custody of authentication material. Assess Authentication Material Custody Integrity; separate private content or other protected information can independently engage this class.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The access finding concerns private repository state and the reported authentication-material chain as protected information or a distinct record modification; any secret-only property is separately assigned to the custody class.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Not aligned exclusion: The observed information operation is validly authorised within the independently established boundary. An approved test does not by itself authorise public release of protected information.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The assessed operation is tested against employee-bound account/repository rights; the precise secret object in the SSO chain remains unidentified. Technical access, research motivation or permission for another target does not authorise crossing this boundary.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Not aligned exclusion: Only a hypothetical vulnerability, exposed endpoint, unverified capability claim or unsuccessful attempt is established, without demonstrated protected-information access, acquisition, disclosure or modification.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The decision relies on the documented operation or named unresolved occurrence fact, not hypothetical severity: Hacktron reports account takeover and creation of a proof-of-access pull request through an employee’s connected Codex. The private repository’s write boundary was crossed through that account route. The proof did not read internal code; access to every connected service is not established. Responsible disclosure and the later bounty do not erase the demonstrated access defect.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Class scope exclusion (all results): The issue is solely accuracy, availability, provenance, secondary-purpose permission or audit reconstruction, without an independently engaged information access or integrity boundary.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The independently engaged property is employee-bound account/repository rights; the precise secret object in the SSO chain remains unidentified; a solely accuracy, availability, provenance or audit result would not suffice.

delta_decisions.basis: Authentication-material custody is materially implicated by the reported account-compromise chain. The available originating account does not identify which protected credential, token or secret left custody. Its demonstrated SSO access is not itself proof of a secret transfer. Neither secret exposure nor verified secret confinement is established.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Identifiable material serves an authentication or authorisation function, or contains the protected secret content needed to exercise that function, in an AI-mediated system or dependent infrastructure.
condition_tests.assessment: The material object question concerns private repository state and the reported authentication-material chain.

condition_tests.literal_condition: An independently evidenced custody boundary governs who or what may hold, receive, disclose, modify or replace the material in the assessed lifecycle stage.
condition_tests.assessment: The governing boundary question concerns employee-bound account/repository rights; the precise secret object in the SSO chain remains unidentified.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Occurrence evidence demonstrates exposure outside that boundary, unauthorised acquisition, or unauthorised custody-changing modification or replacement. Demonstrated retrievability of protected secret content is sufficient without proof of subsequent credential use.
condition_tests.assessment: The originating account must identify the authentication material and whether its secret content was exposed or acquired, rather than merely an identity-flow defect. A redacted technical explanation of the SSO chain or the scoped disclosure report could resolve this. No live credential is required.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Authentication material, its AI-mediated system or dependent infrastructure, and the applicable authorised custody boundary are identified.
condition_tests.assessment: The material object question concerns private repository state and the reported authentication-material chain.

condition_tests.literal_condition: A concrete handling operation, delegation, lifecycle transition or exposure attempt materially tests custody protection.
condition_tests.assessment: The governing boundary question concerns employee-bound account/repository rights; the precise secret object in the SSO chain remains unidentified.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Observed handling or verification shows that the secret remains confined to authorised holders, recipients and pathways, with the applicable protection preserved through the tested operation.
condition_tests.assessment: The originating account must identify the authentication material and whether its secret content was exposed or acquired, rather than merely an identity-flow defect. A redacted technical explanation of the SSO chain or the scoped disclosure report could resolve this. No live credential is required.

condition_tests.literal_condition: The finding is limited to the tested material, operation and stage. Absence of reported misuse, ordinary credential availability, a missing key or an unverified rotation claim does not supply this evidence.
condition_tests.assessment: The originating account must identify the authentication material and whether its secret content was exposed or acquired, rather than merely an identity-flow defect. A redacted technical explanation of the SSO chain or the scoped disclosure report could resolve this. No live credential is required.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Class scope exclusion (all results): The material is only a non-secret identifier, public connection identifier, public verification key or public client configuration that is intended to be available in the assessed context. A separately exposed secret or unauthorised protected-information operation requires its own assessment.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The assessed objects are private repository state and the reported authentication-material chain. Public connection identifiers, fake placeholders and public verification material are excluded; no such object supplies this custody finding.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Class scope exclusion (all results): The issue concerns only coherent propagation of expiry, revocation, refresh or replacement into sessions and dependent operations. Assess Authentication-State Continuity unless a separate custody property is evidenced.
exclusion_tests.assessment: Acquisition, exposure or custody-changing modification is assessed separately from propagation of expiry, revocation or session state.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Not aligned exclusion: Credential handling or delegation is validly authorised and preserves the applicable custody boundary. Mere credential possession or ordinary authorised use is not a custody defect.
exclusion_tests.assessment: Holder/recipient authority is tested against employee-bound account/repository rights; the precise secret object in the SSO chain remains unidentified, rather than inferred from technical possession or the agent’s objective.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Not aligned exclusion: Only a theoretical vulnerability, unverified secret classification, unusable placeholder or unsuccessful attempt is shown; protected authentication material is not demonstrated outside custody.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The accepted finding relies on the identified secret object and documented custody event. For Boundary, The originating account must identify the authentication material and whether its secret content was exposed or acquired, rather than merely an identity-flow defect. A redacted technical explanation of the SSO chain or the scoped disclosure report could resolve this. No live credential is required.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Not aligned exclusion: Material is already invalid and no residual secret-protection or custody obligation is independently established. Do not assume every expired token remains a usable secret.
exclusion_tests.assessment: No expired or demonstrably unusable candidate supplies the finding. Working acquisition/use or the specifically unresolved secret identity bounds the decision.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Class scope exclusion (all results): The only property is the scope of an action performed using a credential, without a distinct custody issue. Assess the applicable authority or action class.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The decision addresses acquisition, exposure or custody-changing modification of authentication material; later action scope is not substituted for this event.
